title: Dynamic curve · Positioning the mark
slide_intent: Teach designers to adjust the prominence of the mark to the viewing task. A small identifier can sign a printed page, while a sign may need the name itself to lead.
strategic_value: Special Olympics can retain the same curved division across print and signage while varying how much space belongs to the mark.
demonstration: Five print layouts set small marks in white fields along the top, base or side of a blue field. A separate group of three signs increases the mark’s share of the available area.
practical_value: Decide how large the mark should be and which edge can house it. Check the sign examples when the identifier needs to carry the message.

content_islands.name: Heading and usage notes
content_islands.spec: Place the red device name above the gray positioning title. Set two small illustrated notes in the left column, one on protecting the mark and one on sign scale.

content_islands.name: Print placements
content_islands.spec: Under the print label, place two upright samples above a row of three wide samples. Keep the blue field dominant and set the mark in the white area formed by the arc.

content_islands.name: Sign placements
content_islands.spec: Group three sign formats inside a dotted box at upper right. Compare tall, wide and short proportions and enlarge the program mark relative to the print samples.
